description: Recurrent PPO, 12-D observation (10-D LOS kinematics + tracking staleness/uncertainty; no privileged target turn-rate). Trained against the v1 evasion maneuver library (break_turn, vertical_jink, random_jink, bounded_weave) under a delayed/estimated alpha-beta tracking chain (seeker rates feed the velocity channel; see estimation/alpha_beta.py), not ground-truth target state. This supersedes observation_target_turn_rate below on a different, harder, more realistic problem -- that lineage saw exact target turn-rate and a single non-evasive maneuver family; this one sees only estimated tracking and four evasion kinds. Root-cause chain that made this lineage trainable: RewardConfig.t_go_max_s was decoupled from max_time (was leaking a farmable heading-wobble reward via the ZEM shaping potential's lookahead, see NOTES.md 2026-09-14 'Root cause of the shaping_gamma / effort_weight failures'), then extended to CP6 (config nominally caps at 5 checkpoints; run_checkpoint()'s upper bound was relaxed for this experiment, PPOTrainingConfig.total_checkpoints itself is unchanged).

reward_config_deltas_from_default.note: shaping_gamma=1.0, effort_weight=5.0, miss_tanh_scale_m=3000.0 all left at evasive_redesign_config() lineage defaults; zem_t_go_max_s is the only deliberate change from the pre-fix lineage.

held_out_eval_300_case.note: This is the statistically load-bearing number, not the 50-case figure above -- it was run specifically to check whether the 50-case result was noise. It wasn't: hit rate held at 80.7%.

classical_pn_reference_300_case.note: PN consumes the same estimator output the policy sees (information-matched), not ground truth. Fails structurally on break_turn (41/75) and random_jink (41/75); when it fails, it fails by hundreds to >1000 m.

significance.note: Two other seeds pushed through the same config to CP6 did not replicate this hit-rate margin at n=300 (seed4: 73.7%, z=0.28 vs PN, a tie; seed2: 65.3%, z=-1.94, marginally below PN). This is a promotion of one specific checkpoint, not a claim that the zem_t_go_max_s config reliably beats PN on hit rate -- see NOTES.md 2026-09-14 for the full three-seed comparison. What IS consistent across all three seeds, unexceptioned, at both n=50 and n=300: every RL checkpoint's worst miss stayed under 18 m, categorically better than PN's catastrophic-loss tail.

supersedes.previous_best_note: Prior baseline used privileged ground-truth target turn-rate and a single fixed target path (no evasion, no sensor delay/noise) -- this was the original bug report that started the evasive-tracking redesign (docs/evasive-tracking-redesign-spec.md). Kept for comparison; not deleted.
